tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Tonight on the Exchange Report: the Fronge transaction log that nobody has fully untangled, what Crownline's waiver activity says about a roster already built to win, and whether SDR's pick-hoarding strategy has finally crossed from 'disciplined' into 'delusional.' Terrence has a verdict. Dexter says he already called it. Seven o'clock.

tweets.name: Clara Hopkins
tweets.text: Quick inventory of where we actually are right now: Apex is stacked and QB-fragile, Crownline is quiet and ominous, Obsidian is trimming without replacing, Sovereign is hoarding picks while releasing receivers, and Fronge is in Cuba. Tonight's show writes itself. We're live at seven — Vivienne, Terrence, and Dexter are already arguing about Brent in the group chat.

tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: Adam adding Damien Martinez thirteen days ago got exactly zero coverage from anyone at this network. Martinez is sitting behind a real opportunity in Green Bay. I flagged the GB backfield situation before the rookie draft and apparently everyone forgot. HLX at $95.11 is not an accident — the quiet adds are part of why Helix's turnaround story has legs.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: The Corbishley-Fronge trade from six days ago doesn't get enough credit for what it means at the depth level. Fronge getting Diggs is a win on paper, but they just released Tyler Huntley — a QB6-7 in superflex terms — the same day and haven't replaced him. That room has a Diggs-shaped highlight on top of a roster construction problem underneath.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: Brent releasing Emari Demercado and Diego Pavia in the same window eight days ago would be unremarkable housekeeping on any other roster. On Obsidian — where you already cannot buy a win projection and your entire valuation story runs through one tight end — trimming without adding is not roster management. It is hoping. And hope is not a business strategy.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: Charles quietly added Malik Benson and Roman Wilson off waivers eight days ago and basically nobody said anything about it. That's how good Crownline's roster already is — the additions that would headline anyone else's week are just footnotes. CROWN at $131.71 and championship-or-bust energy radiating off every single transaction. I respect the pressure they're operating under.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: Fronge is in Havana with zero pick liquidity, just traded away Stefon Diggs, added an RB named Seth McGowan off waivers, and FORG is sitting at $90.38 like everything is fine. I need someone to give me a segment on this roster because from the outside it looks like the business equivalent of ordering soup in a hurricane.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: APEX at $115.51 is the only number on the board I want to talk about today. Corbishley added Braelon Allen six days ago, has Burrow, Hall, Montgomery, Higgins — and the market is STILL undervaluing the QB situation because there's no true QB1 locked in behind Burrow. One injury and that whole beautiful machine has a crisis. Which is why I am a BUY with a very loud asterisk.

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: The Wingard cut of Beaux Collins four days ago is still sitting with me. Collins wasn't a cornerstone, but Sovereign Draft Reserve is already thin on production — they keep stacking picks and releasing the few young receivers they actually have. I'm told internally there's no replacement move imminent. That's the part that concerns me.
